newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to auction Black Sea free trade zone land.
newsitem.headline: Romania to auction Black Sea free trade zone land.

text.p: Operators of a free trade zone in Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta will hold a public tender next month to auction land leases, zone administrators said on Friday.
The tender, open to Romanian and foreign individuals and corporate customers, is scheduled for October 24 in the Black Sea resort of Mamaia.

RA Administratia Zonei Libere Constanta Sud, which manages an area of 187 hectares (463 acres) in the port of Constanta, offers land and sites for industrial activities, trade and services, which can be rented, leased or managed under association accords, a statement said.
Under a 1993 law, local and foreign investors are allowed to lease land and buildings within Romania's six free trade zones for periods of up to 50 years.
Businesses in the free trade area are exempt from customs and excise duties and profit and value added taxes and can repatriate capital and earnings.

Constanta port is a strategic gateway into Europe, with access through the Danube, Rhine and Main rivers. It is located at the crossing of major European and Middle East trade routes and near the big markets of Russia and Ukraine.
